It was also nice to find that even though hacking a Tallneck reveals a ton of shit on the map, it doesn't reveal everything, and deviating from the waypoint path to check out that "empty" spot on the map can turn up new villages, "dungeons," and side-quests. On the one hand, I haven't gotten anywhere that I've gotten stuck/haven't been able to jump/crouch out of, but on the other hand, if it's going to put me on a path "out of the game area," then don't let me jump up there and don't show it on the map (granted, it was a tricky bit of maneuvering to climb the robo-arm, but they should have expected people to try anything to reach a visible section of map).

The second part is what bothers me about a lot of games, in that there are so many things you can see that are simply off-limits because it didn't fit into the "plan" the developers have for players. It's the reason I can't stand the Uncharted series, for one. If you do one thing out of order or try to improvise from the script, it's game over and time to try again until you do it right. These massive worlds that stretch on forever only to end in an invisible wall piss me off to no end. I'm admittedly only about 5 hours into Horizon, so I haven't seen any of the really cool stuff yet. I've been mostly just exploring and enjoying the graphics at 4k with HDR, which are incredible. It just contains a lot of the issues I've had with other open world games in the past, though it is very, very polished. If you're playing on a Pro, I'd be interested in the difference between "resolution mode" with the checkerboard 4K, vs the "performance mode" which gives slightly better effects and draw distance. On a Pro. The differences between the two are minimal, and I actually find the resolution mode to be a more reliable mode as performance mode has more issues with frame rate fluctuation. Similar to how variable mode in Nioh is more erratic than movie mode. It may run at a lower framerate overall, but it's more consistent. I checked both out and resolution-wise, I didn't notice much difference. There was a little bit more shimmer and aliasing in the performance mode, but it's fairly negligible. I admit that while I'm a bit of a videophile, I don't go that in-depth with it. I just play or watch in whatever mode looks best to me, and frame rate is one of those things that I don't focus on because I grew up with abysmal frame rates on the NES, SNES, N64, etc.

My eyes aren't as well-trained as, say, Digital Foundry. Either mode looks great, but if a TV is capable of 4k, resolution mode will definitely look better, even marginally.
